coverage_notes:
WHAT IS FULLY RECOVERED
- Head coach and all nine full-time on-field assistants (the NCAA maximum in 1997). Two independent sources agree exactly: the 1997 Nebraska Football Media/Recruiting Guide staff directory (guide p. 3) and the Wikipedia team-season roster footer, with HuskerMax's 1997 roster page as a third confirmation for the six unlinked names. There were no additional on-field coaches.
- Both graduate assistant football coaches: Chad Stanley (offense/receivers, documented in the 1997 guide) and Jon Bostick (secondary). Bostick is the one genuinely tricky row: the August 1997 preseason guide still lists him as a development officer, so his 1997 service is documented only retrospectively, via the 1998 media guide ("Jon Bostick is in his second season as a graduate assistant coach on the Nebraska football staff" + "In Bostick's first season on staff... the NU secondary helped limit Heisman runner-up Peyton Manning to 134 yards passing in the 1998 Orange Bowl"). That sentence places him on the sideline at the championship game, so he satisfies the ring rule.
- The full-time strength staff: Boyd Epley plus the nine full-time Nebraska Performance Team members the guide enumerates by name and title, plus the eight named 1997-98 Performance Team graduate assistants.
- Football operations, secretarial, equipment, video/film, athletic medicine, and football media-relations tiers.

WHAT I COULD NOT RECOVER
- No "analyst" or "quality control" staff exist for this row. Those job categories did not exist in 1997 Division I-A; NCAA limits were 9 full-time assistants + 2 GAs, and no such titles appear anywhere in either media guide. Zero analysts/QCs is a real finding, not a gap.
- The Wayback Machine athletics-site directory could not be used: the CDX API for huskers.com 1996-1999 returned a 504 gateway timeout, and the modern huskers.com 1997 roster page lists only three coaches (Osborne, Ron Brown, Turner Gill), so it added nothing. Source tier 2 is effectively a miss; tiers 1, 3, and 4 carried the work.
- Football student managers are referenced ("student managers" under Logsdon's duties) but never named in the guide. Not recovered.
- Undergraduate football assistants for 1997 are not named. The guide names one only retrospectively (Stanley served as an undergraduate assistant in 1996).
- The Performance Team org chart (guide p. 66) also names Art McWilliams (Food Service Manager), Linda Ybarra (Office Manager) and Karen Cook (Secretary). I excluded them as rows because the OCR renders that chart as scrambled fragments with no faithfully copyable name+title string, and their roles are athletic-department administration rather than football staff.
- Twenty student athletic trainers are named on guide p. 83 (seniors Aaron Bott, Stephanie Cummins, Karen Hilts, John Myers, Josh Nichter, head student trainers Jim Ohrt, Shawn Pohlman, Brent Todd, and juniors/sophomores). I excluded them as student labor serving all 700 NU student-athletes rather than football staff. Likewise the SID office's graduate assistants (Jeff Griesch, Shamus McKnight) and six named student assistants.
- Athletic-department-wide administrators who are in the football guide but are not football staff were excluded: AD Bill Byrne, associate ADs Fouraker/Hibner/Selig, academics (Leblanc, Zimmer, Hicks, Kuchta, Schellpeper), development (Pierce, Bostick's old office, Blanck, Meyers), marketing, ticketing, licensing, facilities/grounds (Bill Shepard maintains the football practice fields), and HuskerVision (Jeff Schmahl, Shot Kleen, Rick Schwieger, who work with the football film crew). Flagging these by name so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent.
- No mid-season arrivals or departures are documented for any 1997 on-field coach. Osborne announced his retirement on Dec. 10, 1997 and Solich was named his successor the same week, but both worked the Jan. 2, 1998 Orange Bowl, so neither gets a mid-season note.

QUOTE-MATCHING CAVEAT — PLEASE READ BEFORE VALIDATING
Most quotes come from two scanned PDFs whose text is an OCR layer, not born-digital text. Every quote was string-matched programmatically against my own extraction (PyMuPDF for the 1997 guide, Internet Archive's djvu.txt for the 1998 guide) and all passed, but a different extractor may tokenize the same page differently. Two consequences:
1. Quotes reproduce OCR errors verbatim, on purpose. "Assistant Coacli/Offensive Line: MiltTenopir", "Senior Associate A.D./Compliance/Eootball: A1 Papik", "Dr. Lonnie A1 bers", "Assistant Director of Athletic Peformance" — these are what the text layer actually says. I did not clean them, per the verbatim requirement. The role field carries the corrected wording and each source note flags the discrepancy.
2. Many quotes stop at an awkward point because the OCR layer hard-wraps mid-sentence and I would not span a line break. Where a quote alone looks thin, the source note gives the full printed sentence.
Wikipedia quotes (the season/role lines such as "17th season as DC/DL coach") are single-line and should match cleanly. George Darlington's Wikipedia quote is only "DB coach" because Wikipedia gives him no season ordinal; his media-guide and HuskerMax quotes carry the person+role claim.

SCOPE CAVEAT
Nebraska's strength staff and athletic-medicine staff were department-wide units serving all 22-23 varsity sports, not football-only employees. I included them because the football media guide presents them as the football team's support staff and because Epley's unit is conventionally counted, but a stricter football-only definition would drop the Performance Team GAs, Cindy Barker (women's basketball), Brad Brown (track and field), and the six athletic-training GAs. Each of those rows carries a source note saying so, so they can be filtered without re-research.
